jobs.title: Branch Operations Manager, Floorcovering
jobs.description:
The Branch Operations Manager works with the Branch Manager to organize, plan, and implement strategies in a Sherwin-Williams floorcovering branch. This includes supporting all aspects of branch operations, including customer service, marketing, merchandising, inventory, finances, and safety. This role will assist in supervising and training staff and be responsible for contacting customers to generate sales leads.

This position’s typical schedule is 44 hours per week, which may include evenings and/or weekends.

This position is also eligible for bonus based on performance and subject to the terms of the Company’s applicable plans.

This position is eligible for health benefits, such as medical, dental and vision coverage, Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs), disability coverage, security, retirement and saving benefits. Additional benefits include a generous time away from work package, including personal leave, paid parental leave, medical leave, vacation, and holidays.

Job duties involve contact with customers, which may include minors; and access to cash and other payment methods, electronic equipment, personal information, store merchandise and other items of value, and such access may be supervised or unsupervised. The Company therefore has determined that a review of criminal history is necessary to protect the business and its operations and reputation and is necessary to protect the safety of the Company’s customers, staff, employees, vendors, contractors, and the general public.
Minimum Requirements:
- Must be at least eighteen (18) years of age
- Must be legally authorized to work in the country of employment without needing sponsorship for employment work visa status now or in the future
- Must have a valid, unrestricted Driver’s License
- Must have at least a High School diploma or GED
- Must be able, with or without reasonable accommodation, to retrieve material from shelves and floor stacks and lift and carry up to 50 lbs. frequently and up to 70 lbs. on occasion

Preferred Qualifications:
- Have at least one (1) year of experience working in a retail, sales, or customer service position or have completed a Sherwin-Williams Management Training Program
- Have at least one (1) year of experience in leadership role(s), supervising others, or leading teams
- Have previous work experience selling floorcovering and/or floorcovering products
- Have work experience using timekeeping and/or customer relationship management (“CRM”) systems
- Have an associate's degree or higher in business, sales, or marketing
- Willingness to relocate for future job opportunities
- Ability to read, write, comprehend, and communicate in more than one language
- Ability to read, write, comprehend, and communicate in Spanish

#PSGNP
- Support business strategies to increase sales and optimize profitability
- Ensure high levels of customer satisfaction through excellent service
- Build and maintain knowledge of all products to ensure effective customer recommendations
- Build positive relationships with wholesale and retail customers
- Complete store administration
- Ensure compliance with policies and procedures including safety, loss prevention, and security
- Maintain outstanding store condition and visual merchandising standards, including promotional packages and sales floor displays
- Support employee training, development, performance management, and corrective action
- Respond to and resolve any customer and/or employee complaints
- Partner with Store Manager to make outside sales calls to increase market share
The Branch Operations Manager works with the Branch Manager to organize, plan, and implement strategies in a Sherwin-Williams floorcovering branch.

jobs.title: Finance Manager, Budget and Incentives PSG
jobs.description:
The PSG Finance Manager of Budget and Incentives works closely with a variety of functional areas within the Company spanning various levels of the organization. This role manages a segment of the global incentive compensation budgeting process from end to end and has responsibility over ensuring that the Company’s incentive compensation budget policies and procedures are implemented and maintained throughout the year, driving accurate incentive forecasts and payouts.
Because this role involves access to confidential financial information, the Company has determined that a review of criminal history is necessary to protect the business and its operations and reputation and to provide similar protections for its clients and potential investments.
This position is not hybrid/remote and will be located at our Global Headquarters in Cleveland, OH.
Because this role involves access to confidential financial information, the Company has determined that a review of criminal history is necessary to protect the business and its operations and reputation and to provide similar protections for its clients and potential investments.
POSITION REQUIREMENTS
Required:
- Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting, Finance, or Business Administration with a focus in Finance or Accounting.
- 5+ years of experience in  Finance or Accounting
- Advanced experience with Microsoft 365 Suite
- Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship now or in the future for employment visa status
- Must be at least eighteen (18) years of age

Preferred:
- Master’s in Accounting/Finance or CPA .
- Experience in budgeting for incentive compensations.
- Experience analyzing data, present findings, and offer proposed solutions.
- Experience using OneStream and Oracle applications.
- Experience with P&L management and budget development.

Travel: 10%
CORE RESPONSIBILITIES AND TASKS
- Develop, coordinate, and maintain the financial operating systems surrounding the annual incentive compensation budget process for PSG to ensure budgets are accurate and in alignment with the Company’s strategic goals and objectives.
- Maintain a consistent and streamlined incentive month-end close and forecasting process that will be used to provide clear visibility of financial projections, control costs, and prevent unforeseen impacts to key stakeholders.
- Manage the timely and accurate publication of monthly financial incentive results to allow management to react and adjust based on results and develop enhancements that will allow business unit to better drive strategy and profit
- Possess a strong understanding of US GAAP to own the PSG bonus close activities and ensure accurate on time month-end close entries
- Own forecast scenario modeling to provide forecast options based on historical data and trends
- Calculate and track incentive programs in conjunction with HR and business partners.
- Actively manage PSG incentive compensation budget adjustments to ensure accuracy is maintained throughout the year
- In addition to the tasks listed above, this position will gain exposure to reporting and hierarchy changes related to the Company’s global system integration projects and will help drive continuous improvement by employing transactional lean concepts to improve the budget and incentive processes.

The ideal candidate will demonstrate a strong work ethic, ability to work well under pressure, and the skills to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced work environment. Strong organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to adjust and reprioritize as needed, while maintaining a strict adherence to deadlines is critical. Attention to detail, as well as a desire and ability to solve problems through complex financial situations is a must.
The Enterprise Financial Planning & Analysis, Budget and Incentives team provides centralized budgeting and incentive tracking for Sherwin-William’s global businesses. This includes partnering with the company’s business units to develop and maintain accurate expectations of business drivers that enable business strategy and action.

jobs.title: Design Continuous Improvement Leader
jobs.description:
The Design Continuous Improvement Leader will lead the Design Continuous Improvement function for Performance Coatings Group (PCG), integrating Design for Six Sigma (DFSS), continuous improvement, business process design, data analytics, and strategic customer problem solving.
The Design Continuous Improvement Leader will build a scalable, business-unit-focused operating model that applies customer-critical requirements, disciplined experimentation, statistical methods, digital tools, and structured governance to improve product-development speed, robustness, quality performance, and profitable growth. This requires partnering across R&D, Quality, Operations, Sales, Technical Service, Procurement, Legal, regional teams, and customers to convert business needs into measurable improvement priorities and sustainable standard work.
Job duties include contact with other employees and access to confidential and proprietary information and/or other items of value, and such access may be supervised or unsupervised. The Company therefore has determined that a review of criminal history is necessary to protect the business and its operations and reputation and is necessary to protect the safety of the Company’s staff, employees, and business relationships.
This role is not remote/hybrid. This role will report to Sherwin-Williams Morikis Global Technology Center located at 6745 Miller Road, Brecksville, OH 44141.
10% Travel
Minimum Requirements
• Must be legally authorized to work in the country for which you are applying for employment (without now or in the future needing sponsorship for employment work visa and/or permanent residence status)
• Must be at least 18 years of age
• Bachelor's degree in engineering, science, technology, operations, quality, or a related field.
• 8 years of leadership experience in R&D, Quality, Operations, product development, or continuous improvement, including responsibility for complex cross-functional and multi-site initiatives.
• Demonstrated experience designing and delivering technical training, mentoring certification candidates, managing improvement portfolios, and coaching leaders and project teams.
• Advanced analytical and problem-solving capability, including DOE, MSA, FMEA, statistical modeling, data visualization, and appropriate statistical software.
• Executive-level communication, facilitation, change leadership, project/program management, and stakeholder-influence skills.
• Experience working across regions or global teams and willingness to travel as business needs require.

Preferred Qualifications
• Advanced degree
• 10 years of leadership experience in R&D, Quality, Operations, product development, or continuous improvement, including responsibility for complex cross-functional and multi-site initiatives.
• Black Belt certification or equivalent mastery of DFSS, DMAIC, Lean, advanced statistics, and structured problem solving required and Master Black Belt certification

Successful candidate will be required to sign an Employee Restrictive Covenant Agreement where permitted by law.
- Develop and execute the PCG Design Continuous Improvement strategy, roadmap, governance cadence, portfolio priorities, and measures aligned with business and customer needs.
- Lead the global DFSS program, including Champion training, Yellow/Green/Black Belt curricula, candidate mentoring, certification governance, refresher content, and regional capability expansion.
- Institutionalize design quality practices in product development, including voice of customer, critical-to-quality translation, House of Quality, measurement-system analysis, design of experiments, FMEA, statistical modeling, and robust design.
- Partner with business units to identify high-value opportunities and allocate resources to initiatives with the strongest customer, quality, growth, risk, speed, or financial impact.
- Lead strategic customer and product-quality improvement efforts using DMAIC, accelerated root cause, Lean, Kaizen, value-stream mapping, advanced analytics, and structured experimentation.
- Advance data and analytics solutions using approved citizen-data-science and workflow tools such as Dataiku, Power Automate, SharePoint, Business Objects, and related platforms.
- Drive measurable improvement in complaint resolution and complaint-rate processes, design-program adoption, FMAP maturity, toller governance, and applicable quality standards.
- Provide oversight and partnership for GBMS, ISO 9001 activities, management review, calibration governance, and related R&D quality-system programs, as assigned.
- Establish transparent dashboards and operating reviews for project count, validated savings, opportunity cost, schedule, adoption, compliance, customer outcomes, capability development, and key risks.
- Build an engaged, high-performing team through talent planning, objective setting, quarterly development conversations, recognition, job shadowing, coaching, succession planning, and cross-functional exposure.
- Communicate effectively with senior leaders, business partners, regional teams, and customers; escalate material risks early and recommend practical corrective actions.
- Promote a strong safety culture and comply with all applicable Company policies, quality requirements, and ethical standards.
The Design Continuous Improvement Leader will lead the Design Continuous Improvement function for Performance Coatings Group (PCG), integrating Design for Six Sigma (DFSS), continuous improvement, business process design, data analytics, and strategic customer problem solving.

jobs.title: Finance Analyst, FP&A
jobs.description:
The Enterprise Financial Planning & Analytics team provides centralized planning and forecasting for Sherwin-Williams’ global businesses. This includes partnering with the company’s business units to develop an accurate view and expectation of business drivers enabling business strategy and action.
This position is not hybrid/remote and will be located our Global Headquarters in Cleveland, OH.
Because this role involves access to confidential financial information, the Company has determined that a review of criminal history is necessary to protect the business and its operations and reputation and to provide similar protections for its clients and potential investments.
POSITION REQUIREMENTS
Required:
- Bachelor’s degree
- 2+ years of finance and/or accounting experience
- Experience with Microsoft Excel
- Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship now or in the future for employment visa status
- Must be at least eighteen (18) years of age

Preferred:
- Bachelor’s degree with a focus in Accounting or Finance
- Master’s degree with a focus in Accounting or Finance
- CPA or CMA certification
- Experience in financial planning & analytics or supply chain accounting.
- Experience with manufacturing and/or distribution operations, exposure to and understanding of the principles of Transaction Lean and/or Six Sigma, and experience with OneStream performance management software.

This includes partnering with the company’s business units to develop an accurate view and expectation of business drivers enabling business strategy and action.

jobs.title: Warehouse Operations Manager
jobs.description:
We are seeking an experienced Warehouse Operations Manager in Nassjö to lead our warehousing and distribution activities, ensuring the highest standards of safety, efficiency, and operational excellence.
- Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Operations Management, or equivalent experience.
- Warehousing experience, leadership experience would be an advantage.
- Fluent Swedish language skills and good English language skills
- Strong leadership, coaching, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
- Proven experience driving change and continuous improvement initiatives.
- Strong analytical, commercial, and financial acumen.
- Advanced PC and Excel skills.
- Hands-on, customer-focused, and self-motivated mindset.

If you're passionate about leading people, improving processes, and creating a safe and high-performing warehouse environment, we'd love to hear from you.

#LI-EK2
- Lead and develop warehouse teams, fostering a culture of safety, accountability, and continuous improvement.
- Manage daily warehouse and distribution operations to meet business and customer requirements.
- Ensure compliance with health, safety, environmental, and quality standards.
- Drive operational performance through effective resource planning, inventory accuracy, and data-driven decision-making.
- Analyze operational KPIs and implement improvement initiatives to enhance productivity and efficiency.
- Develop and maintain warehouse procedures, ensuring compliance with company policies and applicable regulations.

jobs.title: Continuous Improvement Engineer
jobs.description:
Drive operational performance through continuous improvement and lean methodologies, leading improvement projects, coaching teams, maintaining KaiNexus data, and supporting a culture of productivity, efficiency, and health & safety compliance. Champion data-driven decision making and support the implementation of standard work and best practices across Operations.
- FORMAL EDUCATION:
Required :
- Engineering degree or equivalent Professional Qualification is preferred.

- Demonstration of formal training in Continuous Improvement Tools.

- KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE:
- Experience of continuous improvement working using and coaching CI tools and techniques.

- Experience of using the TPM framework for improvement within a factory.

- Experience of working in a consumer goods manufacturing environment, ideally FMCG.

- Strong financial and commercial awareness, with a good understanding of all functional areas within the business.

- Demonstration of: strong leadership through influencing and coaching; ability to communicate to all levels; energetic passion for creative but appropriate improvement; enthusiasm and patience to develop others; objective analytical style; a strong team work ethic.

- TECHNICAL/SKILL REQUIREMENTS:
- Advanced PC skills essential.

- Thorough knowledge and understanding of Continuous Improvement tools.

- TRAVEL REQUIREMENTS: Up to 10% of the time

- Salary range for this role is 59k to 70k EUR annually.

#LI-JS2
- All employees are legally responsible for their own health and safety as well as those who may be affected by their acts or omissions. They are also legally required to co-operate in health and safety matters as directed by their employer.

- To improve the performance of Operations by providing constant challenge of the status quo, championing lean philosophy, implementing robust measurement of losses, facilitating the development and implementation of a continuous improvement plan.
- Accountable for the information in our CI project tool KayNexus.
- Report on the progress and support Pillar leads of the Standard Work implementation.
- Increase the transparency of Operations by ensuring robust measurement of losses for all areas of Operations e.g. generation of appropriate loss trees. To perform the duty of gatekeeper for the measurement system.
- Encourage a ‘management by fact’ mindset.
- Increase productivity within Operations by leading usage of the appropriate lean tools (e.g. value stream mapping, 5S, Kaizen to eliminate losses such as delay, duplication, unnecessary movement, unclear communication, incorrect inventory, lost sales and product defects.
- Coach CI project leads and the production team in continuous improvement techniques and help them cascade this approach to their teams to develop a proactive continuous improvement culture. Help ensure that ownership of work is allocated to the lowest appropriate level.
- Develop training programmes and undertake training in the use of continuous improvement tools.
- Challenge the production team to ensure appropriate momentum of improvement.
- Maintain the SW Continuous Improvement Database (KaiNexus).
- Manage project improvement initiatives.
- Performs other duties as assigned.

jobs.title: 2027 Continuous Improvement Intern - East Hartford, CT
jobs.description:
The Operations Intern is “hosted” by the Operations Department at one of our manufacturing/distribution facilities, or headquarters.
The identified candidate will start on May 30, 2027, and end July 30, 2027, at our East Hartford, CT site.
Minimum Requirement
- Must be enrolled in a college or university at the time of the internship or co-op program
Must have at least one (1) year of work experience using Microsoft Office products such as Word, Excel and Power Point
- Must be at least eighteen (18) years of age
- Must be legally authorized to work in the country of employment without needing sponsorship for employment work visa status now or in the future

Preferred Qualifications
- Pursuing a degree in Engineering (e.g. Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering).
- Have previous Sherwin-Williams Internship or Co-op experience
- Have previous experience working in a team-oriented setting including work experience, extracurricular activities, military service, etc.
- Be a rising or current junior or senior in college or university at the start of the internship program
Position Responsibilities include, but are not limited to, assisting the Operations Manager with:
- Observe manufacturing processes with a Continuous Improvement (CI) mindset to identify waste, process variation, safety risks, and operational inefficiencies, while seeking opportunities to improve quality, delivery, cost, and employee engagement.
- Apply Toyota Production System (TPS) principles and Lean tools including Value Stream Mapping (VSM), 5S, Standard Work, Visual Management, Root Cause Analysis, and Problem-Solving methodologies to design and implement improved process flows.
- Facilitate and support Kaizen activities using the "Quick Kaizen" philosophy by encouraging simple, practical, employee-driven improvements that can be implemented rapidly and sustained over time.
- Collaborate directly with operators, technicians, and supervisors to develop solutions, reflecting the Principle of Respect Every Individual and recognizing frontline employees as the primary source of process knowledge and innovation.
- Support the development of a Lean culture through the application of Daily Management concepts and behaviors, including visual management, accountability processes, leader standard work, and continuous problem solving.
- Understand the principles of the Sherwin Williams standard work matrix and how each element, 5S/TAKT/Kaizen/SOP is applied in the factory.
- Engage in early career development programming, including workshops, info sessions, and networking opportunities through the GSC Program Team

What is the Process to get Started?
Step 1 – Digital Interview
Upon review of your application, qualified candidates will be invited to complete a digital video interview via HireVue, our interview partner. The interview will consist of a few behavioral based questions You’ll be able to record and complete your video interview anytime, anywhere! While you can complete this video interview on your own schedule, we ask that this step be completed within 7 days of receiving an invitation.
Step 2 – Hiring Manager Interview
Your video interview is reviewed by a member of our Recruitment team, and our top candidates are invited to meet with our team for a virtual interview.
The Continuous Improvement Intern is “hosted” by the Operations Department at one of our manufacturing/distribution facilities, or headquarters.
